subject: Request: flexible stipend routing for accelerator cohort
messages:
From: Ana Morales <ana@catalystlabs.co>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Catalyst Labs Finance <finance@catalystlabs.co>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: flexible stipend routing for accelerator cohort

Hi Evelyn / Lauren,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — Catalyst Labs is excited about Redwood. One operational question came up from our finance team that will determine how we onboard a cohort next month: the $50k promo credit you offered as part of the accelerator — can that be treated as a monthly stipend (e.g., $12.5k per month over 4 months) and split across invoices to match our grant accounting?

Specific asks from our side:
- Ability to route the stipend to a separate invoice line (so our grants team can proof expenses per cohort month).
- Confirmation whether this stipend counts as vendor credit (non-taxable pass-through) or will be recognized as revenue by Redwood for our W9/accounting.
- Whether the credits can be applied to Dedicated/reserved capacity or are limited to hosted API usage.

I've attached a proposed milestone schedule for our cohorts (catalyst_milestone_schedule.xlsx). Appreciate a quick confirmation of feasibility and any documentation we should include in our PO.

Best,
Ana Morales
Head of Programs, Catalyst Labs
ana@catalystlabs.co

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: Ana Morales <ana@catalystlabs.co>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: flexible stipend routing for accelerator cohort

Ana — thanks for the clear note and the schedule. Quick summary below and two options we can pursue; I copied Lauren who owns billing ops.

Short answer: yes — we can support a stipend-like flow, but the final path depends on whether Catalyst wants credits (consumable, hosted API) or a contractual stipend that maps to invoices and POs. Options:

Option A — Escrowed / Stipend routing (recommended for grants accounting)
- We convert the $50k promo into a "stipend" product and issue four monthly invoice lines (12,500 each).
- Each month will be billed/credited against a separate invoice so your grants team can reconcile month-by-month.
- This requires a short addendum to the SOW (one-page), and we can route invoices to finance@catalystlabs.co as requested.
- Tax treatment: we will provide a statement of credits applied. Ben in GTM/finance should confirm classification; see cc.

Option B — Credit conversion to Dedicated commitment (one-time conversion)
- Convert credits into a discounted reserved capacity SKU. Simpler for us operationally but requires upfront commit and may not fit your grants invoicing cadence.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm which option you prefer.
2) If Option A, we draft an SOW addendum and a mutual action plan (MAP) — I can share a template.
3) Ben/Finance to weigh in on tax/treatment paperwork.

I'm attaching our latest program terms for reference (redwood_program-terms-v3.pdf).

If you want, we can do a 20-min call today to walk billing and grants through the mechanics.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Morales <ana@catalystlabs.co>, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: flexible stipend routing for accelerator cohort

Looping in a few operational details from finance/marketplace perspective. High level: we can do Option A with a couple guardrails so it stays clean for bookkeeping and doesn't create downstream marketplace conflicts.

Notes / recommendations:
- SKU approach: create two dedicated SKUs for this program: STIPEND-ONBOARD (one-time) and STIPEND-MONTHLY (recurring credit). That keeps GL mapping simple for both sides. (I've attached a draft SKU mapping sheet: sku_mapping_sheet.csv).
- Tax/accounting: Redwood will issue credit memos against the invoice lines; we are not treating grant-funded stipends as taxable revenue for the customer. For Redwood's own revenue recognition we'll treat the promotional stipend as contra-revenue (per ASC guidance) — I can share a memo for your accounting team.
- Dedicated eligibility: credits applied to Dedicated are allowed but must be paired with a consumption true-up — if utilization goes beyond the reserved pool, we'll bill overage on the standard rate.
- DocuSign flow: simplest path is a one-page addendum + PO referencing the addendum; we can push to DocuSign once legal signs off: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC-REDACTED

If Catalyst is comfortable, we'll prepare the SOW addendum and the MAP. Evelyn — happy to take point on the memo for their accounting lead.

Thanks,
Ben Carter | Head of GTM Ops, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Ana Morales <ana@catalystlabs.co>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Catalyst Labs Finance <finance@catalystlabs.co>
Date: 2026-08-03T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: flexible stipend routing for accelerator cohort

Thanks Evelyn & Ben — this is exactly what we needed. Catalyst would like to proceed with Option A (escrowed/stipend routing) with the following conditions:
- Monthly invoice lines for $12,500 for Aug–Nov 2026 routed to finance@catalystlabs.co.
- Addendum language that clarifies credits are grant-funded stipends and will be documented as credits/memos for our auditors.
- Confirmation in writing of the overage policy if we convert any portion to Dedicated mid-program.

We'll raise a PO referencing the addendum once you send the DocuSign package and the accounting memo for our records. Please let me know if you need any additional billing info (tax IDs / W9).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — want to finalize before the cohort kickoff next Monday.

Best,
Ana
